draft.title: Sampling
card: A population is the whole group a researcher wants to learn about. A sample is the smaller group taken from it and actually studied.
every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen, such as drawing names from a hat.
the population is split into groups, such as age groups, and people are chosen from each group in the same proportions as in the population.
A sample that represents the population lets researchers generalise, which means applying the results to the whole population. A sample that does not represent it makes generalising unreliable.
draft.remember: Study a sample, but choose it so it mirrors the population. Then results can be generalised.

a.q: Why do researchers try to draw a representative sample from a population?
opts: So the results can be generalised to the population
So every participant gives the same results
So the whole population can be studied directly
So the researcher can predict the results in advance
a.why: A representative sample has the same makeup as the population, so what is found in the sample is likely to apply to the population. It does not make participants give the same results, and a sample is used because the whole population is not studied.
a.clue: Think about what the researchers want to say about the whole group.

b.q: A school has 600 students in Year 7 to Year 12, and 100 students in each year level. Mia wants a sample of 60 that matches the school by year level. Which method does this?
opts: Stratified sampling, taking 10 students from each year level
Random sampling, choosing 60 names from one year level
Stratified sampling, choosing 60 students from Year 12
Random sampling, choosing the first 60 students she meets
b.why: Each year level is 1/6 of the school, so choosing 10 from each year level matches the population and is stratified sampling. Choosing from one year level cannot represent the school, and taking the first 60 students she meets gives some students no chance of being chosen.
b.clue: Which option keeps each year level in the same proportion as the school?

a.best: So the results can be generalised to the population

b.best: Stratified sampling, taking 10 students from each year level

problems.detail: The stratified sampling line says people are 'chosen' from each group but leaves out that they are chosen randomly within each stratum. The VCE Study Design treats random selection within strata as part of the definition, so students could lose marks if they learn this version.

check.summary: Both questions have one clearly right answer and the explanations match the card. The only issue is that the card's definition of stratified sampling leaves out random selection within each group, which VCE expects students to include.
